```{r}
# packages
library(tidyverse)
library(targets)
library(patchwork)

library(INBOtheme)
theme_set(theme_inbo(transparent = TRUE))

# Conflicts
conflicted::conflicts_prefer(dplyr::filter)
conflicted::conflicts_prefer(dplyr::select)

# Paths
mbag_dir <- rprojroot::find_root_file(criterion = rprojroot::is_git_root)
store <- file.path(mbag_dir,
                   "source", "targets", "distance_sampling", "_targets")

# Source functions
source(file.path(mbag_dir, "source", "R", "tar_read_ds.R"))
source(file.path(mbag_dir, "source", "R", "plot_detection_curve.R"))
```

### {{specname_cap}}

```{r}
# To make it easier
params <- NULL
params$species <- "{{species}}"

# Species results not 2023
exclude_2023 <- c("Graspieper", "Grutto", "Scholekster", "Wulp")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-detprob-{{label}}
#| fig-cap: "Detectiecurves voor {{specname_low}}. De stippellijn geeft de gemiddelde
#|   detectiecurve aan."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 11
#| fig.align: "center"
# ---------------------------
# Step 0: Load models and extract formulas/keys
# ---------------------------

# Read the final models from the targets store for the specified species
final_models <- tar_read_ds("model_selection", params$species, store = store)

# Assign names to the models corresponding to years
names(final_models) <- 2023:2025

if (params$species %in% exclude_2023) {
  final_models <- final_models[-1]
}

# Extract the detection function formula from each model
forms <- lapply(final_models, function(model) {
  model$ddf$ds$aux$ddfobj$scale$formula
})

# Determine the key function type (half-normal vs hazard-rate) for each model
keys <- lapply(final_models, function(model) {
  ifelse(
    model$ddf$ds$aux$ddfobj$type == "hn",
    "half-normal",
    "hazard-rate"
  )
})

# ---------------------------
# Step 1: Create detection curve plots for each year
# ---------------------------

# Initialize an empty list to store the plots
plots <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(final_models))

# Loop over each model/year
for (i in seq_along(final_models)) {
  year <- as.character(names(final_models[i]))  # Current year
  ds_model <- final_models[[year]]             # Current detection model
  f <- forms[[year]]                           # Current formula
  form_title <- ifelse(f == "~1", "", paste0(" (", f, ")"))
  title <- paste0(Distance:::model.description(ds_model$ddf), form_title)

  # Generate the detection curve plot
  p <- plot_detection_curve(
    ds_model,
    show_data = TRUE,            # Show observed data points
    plot_average_fit = TRUE,     # Show average fit line
    plot_covariate_fit = TRUE    # Show covariate-specific fit lines
  ) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 0.25)) +
    labs(
      x = "Afstand (m)",
      y = "Detectiekans",
      colour = "",  # Remove legend title
      title = year,
      subtitle = title
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +  # Clean minimal theme
    theme(
      legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "darkgrey"),
      legend.margin = margin(6, 6, 6, 6),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )

  # Store the plot in the list
  plots[[i]] <- p
}

# Assign names to the plots for easy reference
names(plots) <- names(final_models)

# ---------------------------
# Step 2: Identify legend variables for each plot
# ---------------------------

# For each model, extract all variables that determine legend groups
legend_vars <- lapply(final_models, function(ds_model) {
  # Variables in the formula
  vars <- all.vars(as.formula(ds_model$ddf$ds$aux$ddfobj$scale$formula))
  # Unique combinations of covariates
  sort(unique(apply(ds_model$ddf$data[vars], 1, paste, collapse = " - ")))
})

# ---------------------------
# Step 3: Group only consecutive plots with identical legend variables
# ---------------------------

group_list <- list()  # List to store groups of consecutive plots
start <- 1

while (start <= length(plots)) {
  end <- start
  # Extend the group forward if next plot has identical legend variables
  while (end + 1 <= length(plots) &&
           identical(legend_vars[[end]], legend_vars[[end + 1]])) {
    end <- end + 1
  }
  # Store indices of consecutive plots sharing the same legend
  group_list[[length(group_list) + 1]] <- start:end
  start <- end + 1
}

# ---------------------------
# Step 4: Combine plots sequentially with patchwork
# ---------------------------

combined <- NULL       # Initialize combined plot
heights_list <- c()    # To store relative heights for each group

for (grp in seq_along(group_list)) {
  idx <- group_list[[grp]]  # Indices of plots in the current group

  if (length(idx) == 1) {
    # Single plot: just add the legend at the bottom
    p <- plots[[idx]] + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  } else {
    # Multiple consecutive plots: combine vertically and collect shared legend
    p <- wrap_plots(plots[idx], ncol = 1, guides = "collect") &
      theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  }

  # Stack the group vertically in the final combined plot
  if (is.null(combined)) {
    combined <- p
  } else {
    combined <- combined / p
  }

  # Assign relative height proportional to the number of plots in the group
  heights_list <- c(heights_list, length(idx))
}

# ---------------------------
# Step 5: Apply relative heights and display
# ---------------------------

combined + plot_layout(heights = heights_list)
```
